subject: Information Theory
title: Entropy and Key Strength
description: A 60-second lesson on Entropy and Key Strength.

hook.text: Your password is 'password123'. It has 10 characters but nearly zero entropy. A dictionary attack cracks it instantly.

buildup.text: Entropy measures unpredictability. A truly random 128-bit key has 128 bits of entropy. A common password has a few.

discovery.text: Shannon's entropy formula applies directly: H = -Σ p(x) log₂ p(x). More uniform distributions mean higher entropy.

twist.text: Length alone doesn't create security. Seven random words beat twenty predictable characters every time.

climax.text: Key strength equals entropy, not length. Randomness is the true measure of cryptographic security.

punchline.text: Entropy is security. Predictability is the enemy.

quiz.question: Why is 'password123' insecure despite having 11 characters?
options: It has very low entropy—it's highly predictable
